title: Dedicated capacity: load signature calibration and customer onboarding verification kit
creator: Asha Patel
description: Create a reproducible, customer-run verification kit and internal calibration process that defines a deterministic 'throughput signature' for a Dedicated capacity pool. This ticket covers: (1) a lightweight load generator and canonical traffic recipes combining synthetic and small replay traces, (2) a benchmarking methodology that isolates KV-cache warmup, batching behavior, and tail latency under steady-state and burst traffic, and (3) a short, customer-facing acceptance checklist and onboarding runbook for Dedicated capacity sign-off. Goal: reduce onboarding time, provide auditable throughput guarantees, and surface autoscaling policy regressions early.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible load generator (docker image and small CLI) that can be run by customers and internal SRE with a single command
A documented methodology that explains how to measure baseline throughput, warmup curves, and tail latency; includes scripts to compute p50/p95/p99 and token/sec over 1h and 6h windows
Customer onboarding checklist (one-page) and a 10-minute runbook that results in a pass/fail verdict for capacity acceptance
Benchmarks include at least three traffic profiles: latency-sensitive single-stream, mixed chat-like session bursts, and high-throughput embedding batches
Automated comparison step that validates measured throughput against the declared capacity target within a configurable tolerance (default ±10%)
test_plan_steps: Step 0: Provision a mirrored Dedicated pool with versions pinned to the production machine image and runtime-1.22
Step 1: Deploy the load-generator docker image (redwood/load-signature:2026-03) to a client host; validate TLS and API key access
Step 2: Run synthetic microbenchmarks to calibrate per-GPU token/sec baseline for sequence lengths 64/256/1024
Step 3: Replay a 30-minute sampled customer trace (sanitized) at 0.5x, 1x, and 2x declared QPS, record KV-cache hit curves
Step 4: Execute burst profile (90s bursts every 5m) to validate autoscaling triggers and instance spin-up latency
Step 5: Produce a benchmark report; run the automated comparator against the capacity SLA and mark acceptance or list fail reasons
Step 6: If failure: collect kernel-level perf counters, runtime logs (kvcache, batching metrics), and open ENG follow-up with data attached
updates: 2026-03-11: Spike completed for load-generator CLI. Prototype supports synthetic and replay modes. Found that KV cache warmup can take 6-12 minutes for 1024-token sessions; added warmup phase to methodology.
2026-03-12: Design review with PM and SRE; agreed to include a 'customer short-run' (10 minutes) pass/fail path plus an optional 6-hour stress run for contractual verification.
2026-03-13: Chose docker image name redwood/load-signature:2026-03 and uploaded initial artifacts to Drive. Link in 'links' below. Marcus to own CLI UX and docs.

2026-03-14: PR opened for load-generator (github.com/redwood-inference/load-signature PR#482). Early feedback requests: expose kvcache warmup length override and add JSON output for CI parsing. Marked as In Progress and assigned estimate 8 pts.
qa_checks: CLI exits with non-zero code on auth failures and prints structured JSON when --json flag is used
Benchmark report includes raw trace, aggregated metrics, and a human-readable verdict line
All diagnostic artifacts uploaded to S3 path documented in the runbook
Runbook validated in staging with SRE and one pilot customer (engineering contact: Sofia Ramirez)
implementation_notes: We intentionally keep the customer-facing kit minimal: 1 binary, 1 config file, and an optional replay trace. Avoid installing heavy dependencies in customer environments.
Trade-off: Synthetic workloads are deterministic but miss realistic KV cache locality; mitigating by combining small sanitized replay samples with synthetic traffic shapes.
Autoscaling validation focuses on policy gating (scale-up thresholds, cooldowns) and not on cost optimization—cost tuning will follow in a separate ticket.
If measured throughput deviates >20% from target, the automated comparator will produce a 'fail' and include suggested follow-ups (increase pool size, review model variant, tune batching config).
